posts.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
posts.summary: Business and technology leaders need no convincing that the time of agentic AI is here. Organizations are rapidly adopting agents, and few executives doubt the technology’s potential to transform work. But many organizations find that realizing the desired return on investment (ROI) from AI hinges on having the right foundation, with inadequate infrastructure and data…
bullets: Enterprise AI agents currently have access to only 45% of organizational data on average, creating a significant bottleneck for autonomous decision-making.
Gartner projects that AI agents will automate or augment 50% of business decisions by 2027, necessitating a shift away from restrictive legacy data architectures.
Data leaders who provide agents with access to over 70% of enterprise information report higher ROI and greater success compared to laggards who provide access to 30% or less.
Effective agentic AI requires frictionless, real-time integration across structured and unstructured data sources, including supply chain and HR systems, to ensure trustworthy outcomes.

posts.title: Chengdu Auto Show opens next week with nearly 120 brands, 1,600 vehicles
posts.summary:
The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show will cover 220,000 square meters, making it China's first A-level show of the second half of the year.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: - The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show will cover 220,000 square meters, making it China's first A-level show of the second half of the year.
- BYD will have a dedicated group pavilion in Hall 9, with Huawei's HIMA, Xpeng and Nio also attending.

The 29th Chengdu International Automobile Exhibition (2026 Chengdu Auto Show) will be held from August 21 to 30 at the Western China Expo City in Chengdu, Sichuan province, making it China's first A-level auto show...
The show will cover 220,000 square meters and bring together nearly 120 domestic and international brands as well as about 1,600 display vehicles, the organizer said on Wednesday.
As one of China's five A-level auto shows, the Chengdu event is seen as a barometer of demand in the southwestern Chinese market.

posts.title: Hyundai's first Ioniq model for China to open pre-sales at Chengdu Auto Show
posts.summary:
The Ioniq V is the first production model in China from Hyundai's electric brand Ioniq, and will officially launch in September.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: - The Ioniq V is the first production model in China from Hyundai's electric brand Ioniq, and will officially launch in September.
- The mid-size electric sedan was developed under the lead of Hyundai's China design center, tailored for Chinese users and planned for export to global markets.
Hyundai's electric comeback in China is about to deliver its first result.
Beijing Hyundai's Ioniq V will open pre-sales on August 21 at the 2026 Chengdu Auto Show and go on sale officially in September.
That timeline comes from reports by several Chinese auto media, with the September launch previously disclosed by Beijing Hyundai general manager Li Fenggang.

posts.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
posts.summary:
Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: - Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
- The key variable for the second half is the new Sky Nomad product line.

Xiaomi EV, the electric vehicle unit of Xiaomi (HKEX: 1810), delivered 31,267 vehicles in July, up 2.68% year-on-year but down 9.99% from june, according to data released Tuesday by the China Passenger Car...
This marked Xiaomi EV's fourth consecutive month with deliveries above 30,000 units, although year-on-year growth was nearly flat.
The company delivered 30,452 vehicles in July last year.

posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced the industry's first 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to support linear drive optics in high-speed AI infrastructure.
Transitioning to linear optics eliminates the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers, potentially reducing module power consumption by up to 50%.
The new PHY IP addresses critical thermal and latency bottlenecks in dense AI racks, providing a scalable path toward 224G/448G connectivity and co-packaged optics (CPO).

Measured performance data indicates that the IP meets or exceeds OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 specifications for TX VMA, jitter, and RX JTOL, ensuring interoperability in high-speed data center environments.
